side.name: Safety at home
side.line: I don't feel safe with someone in my life.

side.name: Family
side.line: I'm caught in fighting at home.

why.detail: Someone afraid for their safety needs to find that pain without wondering whether ordinary family fights are the same thing. Fighting at home is conflict; not feeling safe with someone is fear of being hurt, and may need crisis resources first.

current.name: Safety at home
current.line: I don't feel safe with someone in my life.

proposed.name: Family
proposed.line: I'm caught in fighting at home.

side.name: Safety at home
side.line: I don't feel safe with someone in my life.

side.name: Relationship
side.line: I'm struggling with my partner.

why.detail: Folding danger into relationship trouble would hide a sensitive pain inside an everyday one. Struggling with a partner is a hard relationship; not feeling safe is about danger, and the person may not be a partner.

current.name: Safety at home
current.line: I don't feel safe with someone in my life.

proposed.name: Relationship
proposed.line: I'm struggling with my partner.

side.name: Loneliness
side.line: Most days I don't talk to anyone who really knows me.

side.name: Plans
side.line: I'd go out more if I had someone to go with.

why.detail: Someone can have close people and still have no one to go out with, so a person can choose between them, more easily if the loneliness line is made concrete. Loneliness is the overall feeling of being alone; the other is wanting company for going out.

current.name: Loneliness
current.line: Most days I don't talk to anyone who really knows me.

proposed.name: Plans
proposed.line: I'd go out more if I had someone to go with.

side.name: Loneliness
side.line: Most days I don't talk to anyone who really knows me.

side.name: No support
side.line: I have no one to call when I need help.

why.detail: Plenty of people with a busy social life have no one they'd call at 2am, and the fixes differ. Loneliness is day-to-day isolation; no one to lean on is having nobody to call in a crisis.

current.name: Loneliness
current.line: Most days I don't talk to anyone who really knows me.

proposed.name: No support
proposed.line: I have no one to call when I need help.

side.name: Belonging
side.line: I don't feel like I belong anywhere.

side.name: Loneliness
side.line: Most days I don't talk to anyone who really knows me.

why.detail: People often feel they don't fit in anywhere while still having a few friends, so the two read differently. Belonging is about fitting into a group or place; loneliness is about missing people day to day.

current.name: Belonging
current.line: I don't feel like I belong anywhere.

proposed.name: Loneliness
proposed.line: Most days I don't talk to anyone who really knows me.

side.name: Belonging
side.line: I don't feel like I belong anywhere.

side.name: Lost community
side.line: I've lost the community I used to be part of.

why.detail: Losing a community you had is a grief of its own, but the two currently share the name Belonging, which the alternatives fix. Belonging is never having found a place; the other is losing one you had.

current.name: Belonging
current.line: I don't feel like I belong anywhere.

proposed.name: Lost community
proposed.line: I've lost the community I used to be part of.

side.name: Intimacy
side.line: I'm missing closeness with someone.

side.name: Dating
side.line: I want a partner and it isn't happening.

why.detail: Someone married can miss closeness without wanting to date, so the two are easy to tell apart. Dating is about finding a partner; intimacy is missing closeness, which people in relationships feel too.

current.name: Intimacy

why.detail: A calm relationship can lack closeness and a close one can be full of fights, so neither covers the other. Relationship strain is conflict or difficulty with a partner; intimacy is missing closeness, with or without one.

current.name: Intimacy

why.detail: Many people want a partner without feeling alone, and many feel alone without wanting to date. Dating is wanting a romantic partner; loneliness is missing people in general.

side.line: Most days I don't talk to anyone who really knows me.

why.detail: Someone who just moved will recognize their situation right away, and the fixes for it are specific. New in town has a clear cause and its own fixes (meeting neighbors, local groups); loneliness can last for years with no move.

why.detail: Knowing nobody at all and knowing people who don't invite you are different situations. New in town is knowing nobody where you live; the other is lacking company for going out, even among people you know.

side.line: Most days I don't talk to anyone who really knows me.

why.detail: Missing old friends is specific enough to choose without thinking twice, and the fix is reaching back out. Drifted apart is losing touch with particular friends; loneliness is the overall feeling of being alone.

side.name: High rent
side.line: I pay too much for housing.

why.detail: Plenty of people pay too much for a decent place, and plenty live somewhere run-down that is cheap, so the choice is easy. Housing is the place being cramped, broken or noisy; High rent is what it costs.

current.name: Bad housing

proposed.name: High rent

side.name: Cold home
side.line: I can't afford to keep my home warm.

side.name: Bad housing
side.line: The place I live is in bad shape, and I can't fix it or move.

why.detail: A drafty, broken home can be cold too, but someone who can't afford the heating bill would look for that pain by name. Heating is not being able to pay to keep warm, even in a sound home; Housing is the place itself being cramped, broken or noisy.

current.name: Cold home

proposed.name: Bad housing

side.line: Everything costs more each year, and my pay hasn't kept up.

why.detail: Going cold at home needs its own fixes, like heating help and insulation, and people living it would look for it rather than a general cost complaint. Heating is one specific cost going without; Rising costs is everything getting more expensive than pay.

current.name: Cold home

proposed.line: Everything costs more each year, and my pay hasn't kept up.
